title_en: The Merit of the Last Ten Nights
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. من حكمة الله جل جلاله أن جعل في الأزمنة والأمكنة مواسم للخير يضاعف فيها الحسنات ويرفع فيها الأجور، وقد جعل الله شهر رمضان أفضل شهور السنة وضاعف فيه الحسنات للمؤمنين، ولذلك تفتح فيه أبواب الجنة وتوصد فيه أبواب النار وتصفد فيه مردة الشياطين، ويقال فيه: يا باغي الخير أقبل ويا باغي الشر أقصر.
body_en: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and His blessings. It is part of the wisdom of God — majestic is His majesty — that He has set within times and within places seasons of good, in which good deeds are multiplied and rewards are raised up. God has made the month of Ramadan the best of the months of the year and has multiplied good deeds within it for the believers; and it is for that reason that the gates of Paradise are opened in it, the gates of the Fire are shut in it, and the rebellious devils are shackled in it, and it is said in it: "O seeker of good, come forward; O seeker of evil, hold back."

flags.note: CRITICAL for display. The record contains the opening formula and a general preamble on the merit of Ramadan, and stops before the last ten nights — the announced subject — are reached at all. A reader would find nothing on the subject the title promises. Style guide section 9; full text behind /medias/doc/d-b-3.docx.

flags.arabic: تفتح فيه أبواب الجنة وتوصد فيه أبواب النار وتصفد فيه مردة الشياطين ... يا باغي الخير أقبل ويا باغي الشر أقصر
flags.context: two pieces of prophetic report woven into the preamble without attribution
options: translate as the Sheikh gives them, with no attribution or grading added
flags.note: Both sentences are well-known prophetic reports, but the Sheikh does not name a narrator, a collection or a grading, and style guide section 4 forbids adding one he did not give. The English therefore carries them exactly as he has them, in his own voice. A reviewer may add an editorial footnote, but it must not be presented as the Sheikh's own citation.

flags.context: the greeting that closes the opening formula
options: typed as a sermon (khuṭbah), in line with the companion record 666 from the same download series
flags.note: The type is not certain. The opening greeting 'peace be upon you' belongs to a lecture or broadcast talk rather than to a Friday sermon, which does not greet the congregation. Against that, this record shares the /medias/doc/d-b-* download series with 666, which is unmistakably a sermon. Typed 'khutbah' on the series evidence; a reviewer who can hear the recording should settle it.

translator_notes: 'مواسم للخير' is rendered 'seasons of good' to keep the Sheikh's agricultural metaphor, which carries into 'multiplied' and 'raised up'.
The du'a and greeting formulae are recited texts; the Arabic is retained in full in body_ar per style guide section 4.
No ruling of any kind is given in this excerpt.
